title: OPTIMIZE YOUR LIFE: Time Management, Productivity Hacks & Energy Budget
summary: NH explains how he fits a 50-hour work week, prolific video output, family and lifting into his life. He treats time as the most valuable resource, schedules on paper with flexible task lists, budgets for active rest, and never sacrifices sleep. Lifting sits at the centre of the schedule.
claims: Everyone has the same 24 hours; hyperproductive people have a strategy while lazy people have none
NH works about 50 hours a week on top of the channel, family and hobbies
Time is the most valuable resource; money is just transformed time
People who say they are too busy to lift usually waste hours, such as 45 minutes scrolling and an hour of Netflix a day
Scheduled active rest, like 45 minutes on the couch after a long day, is not wasted time; unscheduled procrastination is
Rest feels best after strenuous effort, which is why holidays after a hard week are the sweetest
Companies and social media are time leeches competing for your attention to turn it into money
In high school he ran home when school ended at 5 pm so he could lift at 5:30 every day, refusing friends' invitations
Write schedules on paper rather than on a phone; a material copy commits you psychologically. In grad school he survived with daily paper schedules plus a weekly sheet
Lifters who train by instinct without a program will not make the progress they expect
Avoid dependent 'pyramid' task chains; list the day's tasks and do whatever fits each open pocket of time, since flexibility is the key to productivity
Make the first task easy to build momentum, and include leisure items in the list so you always keep moving
The 'work non-stop' grindset meme only benefits the corporations that employ you
Prioritize according to your personality: for him lifting and work come first, then family, and he sacrifices social gatherings
Never sacrifice sleep to get more done; he sleeps 7-8 hours every night
Build the schedule around lifting: if the gym energizes you, train in the morning; if it drains you and your job is cerebral, train at the end of the day
The worst fate for a lifter is slowly giving up the iron because he cannot find the time or energy
